strengths: Well-motivated problem identifying non-differentiable forward operators as a genuine challenge for diffusion-based inverse solvers, with clear analysis of why existing methods fail
Theoretically justified solution: rigorous connection between contrastive similarity and likelihood estimation via InfoNCE and Contrastive Predictive Coding
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with 6 baselines, multiple trajectory density regimes, thorough ablations, and supplementary analyses (t-SNE, uncertainty quantification)
Clear and well-articulated presentation with intuitive figures, particularly Figure 1 demonstrating planner instability
Strong reproducibility commitment: detailed implementation details, promised code release, complete hyperparameter specifications
weaknesses: Limited core technical novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (DPS, InfoNCE, supervised contrastive learning) rather than developing fundamentally new methods
Entirely synthetic evaluation: trajectories generated from A*, trained on synthetic pairs, no validation on real human walking data—undermines claimed practical applicability
Narrow experimental scope: only floorplan inference evaluated despite claims of broader 'spatial inverse problems'; no demonstration on other domains

Circular dependency issue: contrastive training requires approximate forward operator A to generate synthetic data; if A is accurate enough for training, the advantage over direct use during inference is unclear
Practical resolution limitation: capped at 64×64 due to path planner scalability; real-world floorplans require much higher resolution
CFG baseline outperforms CoGuide in dense regime (F1 0.97±0.01 vs 0.95±0.03); dismissal of this result as 'qualitative results do not reflect' is insufficient
Incomplete technical analysis: no approximation error bounds for surrogate likelihood, smoothness claims not quantified, extension to multi-positive contrastive learning briefly justified in appendix
Incomplete ablations: no analysis of alignment loss, embedding dimension, temperature parameter τ; strong sensitivity to λint (Table 2) with no principled selection method for new problems
Intersection penalty is heuristic, not derived from probabilistic model, making generalization to other problems difficult
DMPlug and DiffPIR perform extremely poorly (F1 ~0.28-0.31)—unclear if these baselines are properly tuned, questioning fairness of comparisons

strengths: Novel problem formulation: First to tackle inverse problems with non-differentiable, partially-observable forward operators; well-motivated floorplan application with clear explanation of why standard gradient methods fail
Solid theoretical foundation: Rigorous derivation connecting InfoNCE contrastive learning to likelihood estimation; shows that optimal contrastive classifier recovers likelihood-to-evidence ratio

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multi-baseline comparison (6 methods), evaluation across trajectory densities, ablation studies on key components (intersection penalty, Adam vs SGD, noise robustness), both synthetic and real-world validation
Clear presentation and reproducibility: Extensive implementation details in appendices, promise of code release, informative visualizations, well-organized paper with good algorithmic clarity
Generalization demonstration: Extension to blind audio restoration (Appendix D) suggests applicability beyond floorplans, though preliminary
Thorough ablations: Tables 2-3 and Figure 4 demonstrate careful study of design choices and robustness to noise
weaknesses: Severe scalability limitations: All experiments at 64×64 resolution due to path-planner scalability; acknowledged limitation significantly constrains practical applicability and limits assessment of method's true potential

Limited real-world validation: Only 2 apartments evaluated with no quantitative metrics; real-world trajectories noted to be 'sparser and differently distributed' but domain gap not thoroughly analyzed

Narrow scope despite broad claims: Despite framing as solution for 'spatial inverse problems,' substantive evaluation only on floorplans; audio results feel disconnected and relegated to appendix; no characterization of what problem classes benefit from this approach

Incomplete analysis of contrastive space design: Critical dependence on approximate forward operator A(·) for training pair synthesis; sensitivity to approximation quality not explored; no formal analysis of surrogate likelihood approximation error or error bounds

Unexplained performance tradeoffs: CFG outperforms CoGuide in dense regime (Table 1); this important finding deserves deeper investigation but is merely noted. Best improvements in sparse regime, which may be unrealistic

Theoretical gaps: No formal analysis of likelihood approximation quality; gradient smoothness claimed but not quantitatively demonstrated; training-inference mismatch (multi-positive training vs single-positive inference) inadequately justified
Intersection penalty specificity: Method-specific penalty for floorplan domain (∥y⊙(1−xˆ0)∥₁) contributes substantially to improvement but is not generalizable to other spatial problems

Hyperparameter complexity with limited ablation: Three separate models with numerous hyperparameters; only Table 2 ablates λint; sensitivity to others (ts, te, tstop, τ, λ, encoder architecture) remains unclear
Setup fairness issues: CFG trained on joint distribution (x,y) similar to contrastive encoder; potential baseline tuning gaps; missing comparisons to recent diffusion guidance methods
Missing computational analysis: No runtime or memory comparisons with baselines; computational overhead of contrastive encoder unknown

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear practical relevance: non-differentiable forward operators pose genuine challenges for diffusion-based inverse solvers
Theoretically grounded approach: solid connection between InfoNCE objectives and true likelihood (Eq. 8) provides principled justification for contrastive surrogate
Comprehensive experimental evaluation on primary task: multiple baselines, trajectory density regimes, ablations, real-world UWB validation, and uncertainty quantification
Strong empirical results in sparse regime: consistent improvements when trajectories are most uninformative, with qualitatively superior floorplans vs. baselines
Real-world generalization advantage: CoGuide substantially outperforms CFG when test distribution differs from synthetic training data
Excellent reproducibility commitment: extensive implementation details, code release promised, detailed hyperparameter specifications
weaknesses: Severely limited scope despite broad claims: only 64×64 binary floorplan reconstruction thoroughly evaluated; blind audio restoration relegated to appendix with single baseline and minimal validation; generality claims substantially overstated

Synthetic data distribution mismatch undermines main claims: contrastive model trained on A*-generated trajectories differs significantly from real trajectories; CFG outperforms CoGuide on dense synthetic data, suggesting CoGuide is specialized to synthetic distribution characteristics
Underperforms in practical regime: CFG achieves better F1 scores on dense trajectories (0.97 vs 0.95), which are more common in real applications, limiting practical impact

Confounded experimental contributions: improvements attributable to multiple orthogonal factors (contrastive embedding, intersection penalty ±0.06 F1, Adam optimizer ±0.06 F1, learning rate annealing); no clean ablation isolating contrastive contribution; CFG+CoGuide needed for best results

Significant theoretical gaps: assumes optimal InfoNCE convergence without analyzing finite-training degradation; no robustness analysis for suboptimal embeddings; insufficient justification for multi-positive training extending to single-positive inference; missing characterization of when method succeeds/fails

Method complexity not justified by gains: elaborate pipeline requiring diffusion model (28h), contrastive encoder (12h), CFG model, synthetic data generation, and multiple hyperparameter schedules yields modest improvements (~0.05 F1 in moderate regime)

Real-world evaluation too limited: only 2 apartments tested; UWB trajectories are effectively sparse/noisy, making comparisons to dense synthetic regime unclear; insufficient evidence for practical deployment

Missing critical experiments: no systematic contrastive quality vs. performance analysis; no comparison to other smooth proxies; no cross-domain evaluation; hyperparameter sensitivity (τ, annealing schedule) unexplored; computational costs not compared

strengths: Novel technical contribution: Reformulating likelihood guidance in a learned contrastive embedding space is creative and theoretically justified through connection to InfoNCE
Strong experimental validation for primary application: Comprehensive comparison against 6 baselines across multiple trajectory density regimes with detailed ablations
Solid real-world validation attempts: UWB-measured trajectories and uncertainty quantification (Appendix B) demonstrate practical considerations
Excellent reproducibility: Detailed implementation details in appendices, public datasets, and commitment to open-source code
Well-motivated problem: Clearly identifies genuine challenge of non-smooth, non-differentiable forward operators in diffusion-based solvers
Good presentation with effective visualizations: Figure 1 clearly demonstrates path-planning instability, Figure 2 shows embedding structure
Generalization demonstration: Extension to blind audio restoration (Appendix D) shows applicability beyond spatial problems
weaknesses: Limited practical scope: Restricted to 2D, 64×64 resolution; high-resolution and 3D evaluation absent. Real-world validation minimal (only 2 apartments, qualitative only)
Incomplete generalization claims: Despite claiming broad applicability, only two applications demonstrated (floorplans + audio); no theoretical characterization of operator classes that benefit

Baseline comparison concerns: CFG actually outperforms on metrics in dense regime (IoU 0.95±0.03 vs 0.90±0.06); DiffPIR and DMPlug perform surprisingly poorly, raising tuning questions. Missing comparison with established non-diffusion floorplan reconstruction methods
Synthetic data dependency: Trajectories throughout training/testing generated from A*; unclear how performance degrades when synthetic data poorly matches real-world distribution
Contrastive training requirements: Requires paired (x,y) data despite claims about 'blind' problems; limits applicability to scenarios without such pairs
Domain-specific components reduce modularity: Intersection penalty is floorplan-specific; no clear template for analogous components in other domains
Methodological gaps: Alignment loss (Eq. 12) appears ad-hoc with limited ablation; temperature parameter τ discussed but not analyzed for sensitivity; no convergence guarantees for Adam within DDIM
Missing failure analysis: No discussion of when contrastive guidance fails or comparison of when CFG should be preferred over CoGuide
